jobs.title: GIS Analyst T&D
jobs.description:
About The Role

The GIS Analyst is responsible for the development, maintenance, and quality control of geospatial data and mapping products in support of high-voltage transmission line and right-of-way (ROW) construction projects. This role serves as a core contributor across project lifecycle phases – from preconstruction survey coordination through as-built deliverable production.

Company Overview

Established in 1891, The L.E. Myers Co. (L.E. Myers) – the oldest MYR Group Inc. subsidiary – is recognized as a premier electrical contractor of large utility construction projects across the nation. We are proud to offer our employees the opportunity to complete training, projects, and collaborative learning alongside our family of subsidiaries. We offer stability, with long-term clients and continuous expansion, which allows our tenured employees and new team members space to grow.

At L.E. Myers, we provide structured and strategic occupational growth opportunities for our valued staff. Comprised of long- and short-tenured employees, we are interactive amongst our growing family of subsidiaries, which allows employees to participate in clean energy projects, as well as complete our long-time transmission and distribution projects

Essential Functions

Geospatial Data Management & Mapping
Develop and maintain GIS maps and databases for transmission line construction projects, including structure locations, ROW boundaries, access routes, environmental constraints, and project layers in ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online; continuously update and manage data to support field operations and ensure teams have access to current, reliable information
Produce high-quality maps, exhibits, and spatial deliverables for internal and external project teams
Perform spatial analysis including buffer analysis, route comparisons, conflict identification, and land ownership overlays
Manage and QA/QC geospatial data from multiple sources including survey, LiDAR, aerial imagery, and CAD conversion

Transmission Line & ROW Support
Support permitting teams with accurate construction-specific mapping designs
Coordinate with survey and engineering teams to integrate field data into GIS deliverables and ensure alignment with project design drawings
Update GIS records to reflect field changes and design revisions throughout construction.
Assist with as-built documentation and final record mapping for transmission line projects

Field & Cross-Functional Coordination
Maintain internal GIS users, including onboarding new users, managing permissions, and coordinating ArcGIS Online (AGO) map sharing to ensure appropriate access, data security, and consistent use across project teams
Utilize ArcGIS Field Maps for data collection, field verification, and real-time updates during active construction
Collaborate with Project Managers, ROW agents, Environmental staff, and Survey crews to ensure GIS deliverables meet project milestones
Communicate with client GIS teams to align data standards, projections, and file format requirements

Essential functions of this position are to be performed in a Company-designated office or field location
Regular and predictable attendance
Other duties as assigned
Understand and comply with the Company's Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and other industry-specific professional and ethical conduct standards

ABOUT YOU

Qualifications

Minimum of 3 years of GIS experience with a focus on utility, transmission, or linear infrastructure projects
Experience with coordinate systems, projections, and datum transformations
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:
Experience working for an EPC contractor, transmission contractor, or utility in a GIS capacity
Familiarity with ArcGIS Online, and/or ArcGIS Field Maps for field data collection
GISP certification or ESRI Technical Certification
CAD experience (AutoCAD Civil 3D or MicroStation) for cross-functional data exchange

Preferred Education

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Geomatics, Civil Engineering Technology, or a related field; combination of relevant education and experience considered in lieu of degree

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Proficiency in ArcGIS Pro and/or ArcGIS Online (Esri platform)
Proficiency with geodatabases, feature classes, and geoprocessing tools
Working knowledge of transmission line construction processes, ROW fundamentals, and land ownership data
Ability to read and interpret survey plats, legal descriptions, construction drawings, and one-line diagrams
Strong attention to data accuracy and QA/QC discipline
Knowledge of NERC/FERC transmission standards, NESC structure classifications, or utility asset management frameworks is preferred
Proficiency in MS Office Suite
Strong communication skills, verbal and written
Ability to travel 25%

What We Offer

Compensation & Benefits

Salary
Commensurate with experience, paid weekly. Posted salary ranges are made in good faith. MYR Group reserves the right to adjust ranges depending on the qualifications of the selected candidate.

Comprehensive benefits package - Medical, Dental, Vision, Teledoc, Hearing, Prescriptions, Mental Health, Employee Assistance Plan (EAP), Short Term Disability, Retiree Coverage, and Life Insurance under LINECo – (Low deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums) - Fifteen Dollar weekly premium for employee or employee plus family coverage.

Generous 401(k) Plan with 100% match up to 6%; immediate vesting, and Annual profit-sharing potential.
Superior educational assistance program (support for educational costs, internal training, and more!).
Company-paid short and long-term disability, life, and accidental death & dismemberment.
Company-paid business travel accident insurance.
Various voluntary plans available including supplemental vision, accident and critical illness, ID theft, group legal, group auto & home, and additional voluntary life insurance plans for employee and dependents.

Position may be subject to pre-employment screening, which may include background check and drug testing. Accessibility: If you need an accommodation as part of the employment process, contact our Employment Hotline at 1-855-635-1321.

jobs.description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

Position Overview

Invenergy is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Geospatial Analyst
to join our collaborative Engineering & GIS team. This entry-level role is perfect for individuals eager to grow their technical skills while learning how geospatial data drives decisions across energy project lifecycles.

As a Geospatial Analyst, you will gain valuable experience supporting projects that power homes and businesses. You will learn not only technical GIS workflows but also how those workflows fit into the broader development process—giving you insight into multiple aspects of the energy business. This role is an excellent foundation for advancing into a specialist, developer, or project-focused roles while making a meaningful impact as you learn how energy infrastructure projects are built.

As a Geospatial Analyst, you will be part of a team that supports multiple departments—Development, Engineering, Environmental, and Land—ensuring geospatial data and mapping are accurate, accessible, and useful. You’ll gain exposure to many aspects of the business process, from project siting and permitting to construction and operations.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborative Mapping & Data Support

Work closely with GIS Analysts and Developers to deliver high-quality maps, data, and interactive, online products.
Partner with Development and Engineering teams to meet project needs and deadlines.
Incorporate feedback from multiple stakeholders to refine deliverables.

Project & Workflow Support

Assist with map requests, spatial data integration, and basic analyses.
Support project intake by organizing surveys, parcels, and environmental datasets.
Learn how geospatial workflows contribute to siting, land acquisition, permitting, and design.

Data Management & Learning

Maintain centralized GIS databases with attention to standards and version control.
Learn project geospatial data needs and support holistic data management for project data.
Follow established practices for metadata and file management.
Learn automation and efficiency practices to streamline repetitive tasks.

Team Contribution & Growth

Participate actively in team meetings, knowledge-sharing, and problem-solving sessions.
Build an understanding of how GIS connects across departments and contributes to business decisions.
Actively learn how the GIS team operates and contribute to ongoing improvements.
Take advantage of opportunities for skill development in GIS software, scripting, and renewable energy workflows.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or related field.
Proficiency with ESRI software (ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online / ArcGIS Enterprise).
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to communicate clearly and work as part of a team.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Preferred Qualifications

Internship or academic experience applying GIS in real-world projects.
Familiarity with renewable energy, environmental datasets, or land records.
Exposure to automation tools (Python, SQL) or interest in learning them.
Exposure to raster analysis and image interpretation and processing

Base Pay

$65,000.00 - 79,000.00 USD Annual

Bonus: 15%

The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills.

In addition to base pay, the total annual compensation package may also include eligibility to participate in our bonus program(s) which are designed to reward individual and company performance. Your recruiter can share more about bonus eligibility for this position during the hiring process.

Invenergy offers a variety of other benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k, paid time off, etc.

jobs.title: Environmental Data Management Technician – Mid Level (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
The Role – What You’ll Do

Barr is seeking an environmental data management technician to join our team. In this hybrid role, you will support the Assessment and Remediation business unit. The person in this position will work primarily in the environmental database EQuIS and heavily in Microsoft Excel. Assigned work tasks may include entering data into the EQuIS database; manually checking data thoroughly against original documents; entering geologic data and producing boring logs; producing charts and reports; performing advanced formulas and functions in Microsoft Excel; following processes set by the data management department; and discussing data and projects with other data management staff and project teams.

The ideal candidate for this position is a clear and confident communicator who thrives in both collaborative and independent work environments. They are adaptable, organized, and proactive, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills grounded in scientific reasoning and technical expertise. They bring a high level of attention to detail and demonstrate accuracy and completeness in managing large environmental datasets using tools like EQuIS and Microsoft Excel. For more experienced candidates, leadership, mentoring, and the ability to build strong client relationships are also important. Above all, they value teamwork, quality, and integrity in delivering impactful environmental solutions.

Your Impact – Key Responsibilities

Technical knowledge: apply scientific and environmental knowledge to manage, validate, and analyze large datasets using EQuIS and Microsoft Excel. Use advanced Excel tools such as pivot tables, macros, and formulas to support data-driven environmental projects with precision and consistency.
Project support: contribute to the success of environmental projects by supporting data workflows, coordinating with technical teams, and helping ensure that data deliverables meet project timelines, quality standards, and client requirements. Develop scopes of work, budgets, and timelines according to client specifications and needs.
Problem solving: apply deductive reasoning and scientific thinking to identify data discrepancies, assess data quality, and assist in the resolution of technical issues in environmental datasets. Interpret site data within regulatory and environmental frameworks while contributing to accurate, complete, and meaningful data deliverables.
Communication: prepare clear and concise data summaries, charts, boring logs, and figures for internal use and project documentation. Provide concise status updates to project managers and stakeholders.
Interpersonal savvy: work effectively with various stakeholders to ensure data quality and project success. Show a proactive and professional attitude while learning technical systems and growing within a supportive team environment. 

About The Opportunity

Compensation: anticipated range of $28.90–$36.70 per hour. Compensation will vary based on relevant experience, education, skill level, and other compensable factors. Employees in this position may also be eligible for a discretionary cash bonus based on team and individual performance. This position is classified as non-exempt (hourly) under the Fair Labor Standards Act.
Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position can be based out of Barr's Minneapolis or Duluth, Minnesota, offices.

About You – Required Core Competencies

Education: bachelor’s degree in environmental studies/sciences, geology, chemistry, biology, or a related field.
Experience: 3+ years of professional experience working with databases and advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience with charts, macros, pivot tables and other functions.
Software: strong computer skills, including experience with EQuIS and Microsoft Suite.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future.

Helpful Additional Experience (not Required)

Software: knowledge and experience with the following applications: Access, Python, R, and/or Power BI.
Knowledge of chemistry and/or geology.
Knowledge of state and federal environmental regulations.

Benefits - What We Offer

We are committed to providing an employee experience that attracts and retains top talent. That's why we offer a competitive package of employee benefits - including some unique offerings not found at other companies. At Barr, we also believe that learning doesn't stop when you get your degree, which is why we provide coaching, mentoring, and support for ongoing educational opportunities to foster professional development at every stage of your career.

Competitive, affordable insurance plans: Medical, dental, vision, life, disability, accidental death insurance, and flexible spending accounts for medical and dependent care
Retirement benefits: 401(k) retirement savings plan with company contribution and an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) with company contribution in Barr stock
Profit distribution: Barr has a "no retained earnings" model and distributes all profit to our employees through our annual bonus distribution plan, ESOP, and dividends to shareholders
Professional development benefits: Annual time and expense allowances, mentorship program, and many internal training opportunities
Work/life balance: Paid time off, holidays, overtime for non-exempt/hourly staff, and compensatory time for exempt/salaried staff (time off or pay for extra time worked), paid family leave
Wellness focus: Ergonomic analysis and equipment, Personal Protective Equipment allowance, wellbeing-focused educational opportunities

Please note that benefits eligibility is determined and may change based on part-time, reduced-time, or full-time status.

About Us - Why Choose Barr

At Barr, you'll join a community of engineers, scientists, and professionals who will help you achieve your ambitions and build a meaningful, rewarding career. You'll serve as a trusted advisor to clients who value Barr's tailored solutions and commitment to exceptional service.

As part of our employee-owned firm, you'll contribute to a culture of commitment and camaraderie where staff can thrive as professionals. We value diverse perspectives and experiences and believe an inclusive workplace is critical to our success.

Job Description

AECOM
 has an exciting opportunity for a Mid-level Environmental Planner - Transmission focus
to join our Environmental Planning and Permitting (EPP) team in the Midwest region. This hybrid role offers flexibility and can be based in AECOM’s Indianapolis, Chicago, Columbus, Cleveland, Minneapolis, St. Louis, Kansas City, or Detroit offices, with consideration also given to candidates across the Upper Midwest.

AECOM's EPP team serves numerous private industry and public utility energy clients, on a variety of energy projects including transmission, grid modernization, and renewable energy developments. In this role you will lead or support project teams and work with our environmental planning practitioners and technical subject matter experts to prepare environmental documents, with a particular focus on supporting permitting and entitlement work for our growing line of work with energy developers and utilities. Projects range from regional transmission programs and grid modernization efforts to large-scale renewable energy developments and complex, multi-jurisdictional permitting efforts.

This role would involve serving as a seller-doer, responsible for developing and maintaining client relationships, leading pursuits and project teams, and expanding AECOM's energy permitting and environmental planning portfolio across the Midwest and supporting strategic growth initiatives throughout the U.S.

The responsibilities of this role would include, but are not limited to:

Lead or support environmental planning and compliance efforts for energy infrastructure projects, and coordination and filings with state utility regulatory agencies and public service commissions to support transmission siting, routing, permitting, and certificate approval processes across Midwest jurisdictions, especially within MISO, PJM, and SPP regions. Will include preparation of technical studies and NEPA documentation.

Provide project management on small to mid-sized projects, and support large-sized projects, including developing and tracking project schedules, budgets, invoicing, and coordination with clients, technical staff and subconsultants.
Work on environmental documents and entitlements related to high-profile infrastructure projects, with particular emphasis on energy sector projects.
Support projects across the Midwest and other U.S. markets by leveraging AECOM's national technical and project delivery platform.
Contribute to marketing and business development, preparation of proposals, and formulating proposal cost estimates as a seller-doer.
Mentor and develop junior and mid-level staff by reviewing work products, providing technical guidance, and supporting career development.

Position Summary

The Environmental Engineer is responsible for managing environmental permitting, compliance, and project support for assigned asphalt and emulsions manufacturing facilities. This role serves as a key environmental resource to Operations and EHS teams, ensuring facilities comply with federal, state, and local regulations while supporting operational and capital projects across the company's national footprint.

This position works independently on routine matters and collaborates closely with plant leadership, corporate teams, and regulatory agencies to mitigate environmental risk and support business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance

Manage day-to-day environmental compliance for assigned facilities, including air, water, waste, and spill prevention programs.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulations such as:
Clean Air Act (Title V, minor source, NSR)
Clean Water Act (MSGP stormwater, wastewater, SPCC)
RCRA hazardous and non-hazardous waste requirements

Maintain compliance calendars, records, and reporting schedules.
Lead responses to internal audits, regulatory inspections, and agency inquiries.
Identify compliance risks and develop corrective and preventive actions in coordination with site teams.
Support environmental incident response, investigations, and reporting as needed.

Permitting

Lead preparation, submittal, and management of environmental permit applications, renewals, and modifications.
Evaluate operational and process changes for permitting impacts.
Coordinate technical data collection (emissions, throughput, equipment changes) to support permitting efforts.
Serve as a primary point of contact for routine regulatory agency communications related to permits.
Track permit conditions and ensure operating requirements are communicated clearly to facilities.

Projects & Continuous Improvement

Provide environmental support for capital projects, plant expansions, equipment installations, and process changes.
Conduct environmental reviews to identify permitting or compliance requirements early in project planning.
Support implementation of best practices and standardized environmental procedures across facilities.
Participate in environmental improvement initiatives, including emissions reduction, waste minimization, and operational efficiency projects.
Contribute to environmental data tracking and corporate reporting initiatives.

Collaboration & Leadership

Act as an environmental advisor to plant managers, operations, and maintenance teams.
Partner with Corporate EHS and Engineering on environmental strategy and risk management.
Mentor Environmental Engineer I staff and support training and knowledge transfer.
Communicate regulatory requirements clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field.

Experience

3–6 years of environmental engineering or compliance experience in manufacturing or industrial settings.
Experience supporting multiple facilities or a geographically dispersed footprint is preferred.

Strong working knowledge of environmental regulations affecting asphalt, chemical manufacturing, or heavy industry.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).

Established in 1966, the Chesapeake Bay Foundation (CBF) is the largest regional nonprofit conservation organization dedicated to saving the Chesapeake Bay, its rivers and streams, and the wildlife that call it home. Through our education, advocacy, litigation, and restoration efforts, we work together toward our vision of a healthy and resilient Chesapeake Bay ecosystem where people, plants, and animals thrive together.

In 2014, CBF opened the Brock Environmental Center—one of the world’s most energy efficient, environmentally smart buildings—in Virginia Beach, Virginia.

Advocacy and Restoration

CBF’s Advocacy and Restoration department defends and restores the Chesapeake Bay by protecting the Bay’s natural resources from pollution and other harmful activities by fighting for strong and effective laws and regulations; restoring the Bay’s essential habitats and filtering mechanisms; and involving citizens in CBF’s environmental efforts by recruiting, training, and incorporating them as effective partners and leaders.
